elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: § 10.4 is retained unchanged: "Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I". Ownership remains with Vendor; the redline adds only a licence.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; new § 10.5 is a grant of licence ("M&I grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"), not an assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: § 10.4 ("All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property") and § 17.2 (Customer has no rights in M&I software/systems except as licensed) preserve Vendor's pre-existing IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual grant in § 10.5 is confined to "the Developed Software". M&I's other software, systems and documentation embedded in or needed to exploit that work remain, under the retained § 17.2 tail, licensed only "during the Term to process its data", so there is no perpetual licence to embedded Vendor pre-existing IP; and because Customer does not own the Deliverables the element's premise is unaddressed.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same defect: § 10.5's irrevocability reaches only Developed Software; § 17.2 still limits Customer's rights in M&I's underlying software/systems to Term-only use, with no irrevocable licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: § 10.5 is royalty-free but limited to Developed Software; no royalty-free licence is granted over Vendor pre-existing IP embedded in the deliverables, which stays under the Term-only § 17.2 carve-out.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: § 17.1 (unamended): "Customer shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information", with a broad definition covering all data submitted to or received by M&I for Customer.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: § 17.4 bars M&I from disclosing or using Customer's Confidential Information (which includes all Customer Data per § 17.1) "other than for the purposes contemplated by this Agreement", i.e. performance of the Services; no resale, distribution or independent-exploitation right over Customer Data exists (the § 10.4 resale right is confined to Developed Software). Wording is marginally broader than "solely to provide the Services" but is a genuine use limitation in this services-only agreement.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language; § 10.4 vests sole property in M&I and § 17.1 sole and exclusive ownership of Customer Data in Customer. Condition does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained § 10.4: "All programs (including ideas and know-how and concepts) developed by M&I are and shall remain M&I's sole property." The redline deliberately leaves this intact.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: New § 10.5: "M&I grants Customer a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software"; Developed Software is the defined term for work of authorship created for Customer under § 10.4.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: § 10.5 licence is "to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business"; the conforming "Except as provided in Section 10.5" opener in § 17.2 removes the Term-only contradiction for that licence.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: § 10.5 includes the right to "sublicense the Developed Software for Customer's business".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: § 17.4 confines M&I's use/disclosure of Customer Confidential Information (all Customer Data under § 17.1) to "the purposes contemplated by this Agreement", and no Vendor right to resell or independently exploit Customer Data survives.

reasons: Fallback checklist is position-complete: § 10.5 supplies all four licence modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free) plus use, modify and sublicense for Customer's business over the defined Developed Software, while retained § 10.4 leaves Vendor's generic programs and know-how in Vendor ownership and §§ 17.1/17.4 already satisfy the Customer Data limitation.

Preferred level is not reached and is not claimed: § 10.4 still vests ownership of paid-for work of authorship in M&I, there is no assignment, and the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free grant does not extend to Vendor pre-existing IP embedded in deliverables (§ 17.2 keeps that Term-only). If the drafter wants preferred, it must reverse the ownership sentence in § 10.4 to Customer with an express assignment and extend § 10.5 to Vendor IP embedded in the Deliverables.

Minimal: only two operations (insert § 10.5; add the five-word "Except as provided in Section 10.5" opener to § 17.2). No survival tail, expense language, damages categories, indemnity or procedural boilerplate was added, and no Customer-favourable existing wording (including the § 10.4 refund/credit mechanic and the § 17.4 confidentiality obligations) was deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the § 10.5 cross-reference resolves to a real inserted clause number, no undefined term is created (Developed Software is defined in § 10.4), and the retained § 17.2 Term-only sentence no longer contradicts the new licence because of the express carve-out. M&I's resale right over Developed Software and the refund/credit mechanic survive intact.

Noted but not a blocker: § 17.4's "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is slightly broader than the playbook's "solely to provide the Services"; treat as rationale colour, not a separate deviation.
